alt: A row of jobs, each shown as a letter and its time and weight. Adjacent pairs are compared by cross-multiplying time and weight. An out-of-order pair is swapped and the total weighted cost is shown dropping, an in-order pair is left alone. The row ends sorted by time over weight with the smallest cost, and no swap ever raised it.

steps.caption: Each cell is a job: its letter, then time:weight. The schedule runs left to right, and in this order the total cost is 51. The plan is to fix one adjacent pair at a time.

A and C: 3 x 2 = 6 is more than 4 x 1 = 4, so C belongs first. Swapping lowers the total from 41 to 39.
A and D: 3 x 1 = 3 is more than 1 x 1 = 1, so D belongs first. Swapping lowers the total from 39 to 37.
B and C: 2 x 2 = 4 is at most 4 x 4 = 16, already in order. The total stays 37.
C and D: 4 x 1 = 4 is more than 1 x 2 = 2, so D belongs first. Swapping lowers the total from 37 to 35.
B and D: 2 x 1 = 2 is at most 1 x 4 = 4, already in order. The total stays 35.
No adjacent pair is out of order. After 4 swaps the order is B D C A and the total is 35. No swap ever raised it, so any starting order ends here.
